title: Lydia by the river (Acts 16:1–15)
hookLine: a women's prayer meeting by a river, and one opened heart
tomorrow: beaten, feet in the stocks, and it's midnight. what would you do?

cards: Plan A falls through. Plan B falls through. Then the answer shows up at night.
Acts says Paul and his companions were "forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia," and when they try for Bithynia, "the Spirit suffered them not."
Then a vision: "There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us." So they sail. Here's the odd part.
The dream showed a man begging for help. Who's waiting when they land? Not a man at all.

teach.h: BY A RIVER SIDE, ON THE SABBATH.
teach.b: They reach Philippi, and on the sabbath, in the narrator's own words: "we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither."
Notice that we: from the vision on, the telling slips into first person, as if the writer is on the riverbank too. No building, no crowd.
One woman is named: "a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God." A businesswoman from somewhere else, already praying with this little group.
So the puzzle has an answer of sorts: Acts never explains the gap between the dream and the riverbank. It just goes where people are already praying.
Then the line the day hangs on: she "heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul." Paul speaks; the Lord opens; Lydia listens.
Acts gives the opening to God, not to the speech.

She's baptized with her household, and straight away she turns host: "come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us." She insists. Some readers call this the start of the church in Europe.
Acts tells it small: a riverbank, a few women, one opened heart, and then an open door.

how: Christians gather to pray in small groups, in homes and outdoors as well as in church buildings; Acts 16 tells of one such gathering by a river outside Philippi.

games.q: what does “lydia by the river” mean?
o: a queen of Macedonia who welcomed Paul
a prophetess who first called Paul over
a merchant woman who listened by a river

games.q: who's by the river — tap the pairs.
p: where prayer was wont to be made

s: Lydia was won over by a great sermon
Acts says the Lord opened her heart, so that she attended to what Paul said.
the man from Paul's vision met him when he landed
Acts never shows him. the first people they find are women praying by a river.
Lydia insisted Paul's group stay at her house
come into my house, and abide there. and she constrained us.

games.q: your cousin starts a lunchtime prayer group at work. three people come. she's embarrassed and wants to cancel until more sign up. what fits today's story?
o: keep it; in Philippi it starts with a few by a river.
pause it until there's a bigger room and a real speaker.
fold it into the big Sunday service instead.
games.why: Paul dreamed of a man asking for help and found a handful of women at prayer. Acts tells that small start without apology.

practice: Pick up your phone and text two or three people you'd gladly sit beside on a riverbank, one short line: thinking of you today, anything on your mind?
If you pray, you can hold each one before God as it sends; if not, just keep their faces in view for a moment.

wordCard.voice: Lydia by the river. A seller of purple from Thyatira, praying with a few women outside Philippi, whose heart the Lord opened.

orig.note: Greek: opened, the word in Acts 16:14, whose heart the Lord opened.

carryVoice: Your line: the Lord opened her heart. Paul spoke; God did the opening. See you tomorrow.
